text:
alex: heads up — hosted API p95 jumped from ~180ms -> ~1.2s around 10:12 UTC. dashboard: https://dash.redwood/hosted/p95 (links) :eyes:
maria: yep seeing p99 spike too, rate of queued requests up, backlog on cpu/gpu queues :/
tony: grabbing logs. prelim: kernel-selector started routing a large fraction of short-seq requests to aux-kernel_v2 after the 10:08 deploy
jen: batch histogram shifted massively toward batch size 1-2, mean batch size dropped from 6 -> 2. more per-request overhead.
alex: any recent changes to kselector or sampler?
devops-bot: deploy notice: heuristics-optimizer v1.4 rolled at 10:08 UTC (by ci/cd). changelog: adaptive-kselector tuning + sampler fallback thresholds.
sam: quick tail of runtime logs, filtered:
```
2026-03-20T10:09:04Z KSELECTOR info model=redwood/llama13b seq_len=16 chosen=aux_kernel_v2 reason=latency_heuristic
2026-03-20T10:09:04Z BATCHER debug alloc_batch_size=1 observed_delay_ms=12
2026-03-20T10:09:04Z KV_CACHE warn eviction_ratio=0.41 pool=hosted-primary
2026-03-20T10:10:30Z KERNEL_INIT warn kernel=aux_kernel_v2 cuda_fallback=true
```
sam: looks like aux_kernel_v2 does a CUDA fallback path more often for these short sequences, which increases latency for small batches. also KV cache evictions spiked which could be causing extra priming.
maria: queue depth metric: hosted-primary queue depth for model=llama13b went from 3->27 at the same time window. ratecap shows small issuer bursts but not full throttle.
jen: profiler snapshot (flame + perf): most wall time spent in kernel_init and cublas setup when aux kernel is chosen, and we see extra memory copies due to cache misses.
```
(small ascii flame): kernel_init ~42% | cublas_fallback ~18% | batching overhead ~10%
````

tony: hypothesis: adaptive-kselector heuristics now prefer aux_kernel_v2 for short sequences to reduce cost, but it mispredicts because batch sizes collapsed -> aux kernel enters fallback slow path + KV cache thrash adds priming penalty -> p95/p99 blowup. also noisy tenant observed: tenant-42 had a burst of tiny requests at the same time.
alex: mitigation options: 1) pin kselector to main-kernel-v1 for affected pool, 2) raise sampler coalescing delay to get larger batches, 3) throttle tenant-42, 4) rollback heuristics-optimizer. which fastest?
maria: I can throttle the tenant quickly (policy apply) and bump sampler delay for hosted-primary. low blast radius.
jen: pinning kernel is fast too (runtime config flip). rollback requires CI + deploy, slower.
ton y: I'll apply pin + throttle as quickstop. will also capture flame profiles pre/post.
tony: command run -> `redctl runtime set-pool-config hosted-primary --kselector=main-kernel-v1`
(devops-bot): action: config-update accepted, change-id cfg-20260320-11
maria: applying tenant throttle -> `redctl tenants throttle tenant-42 --qps 5`
(devops-bot): action: throttle applied -> tenant-42 @ 5qps
jen: bumped sampler coalesce delay from 8ms -> 25ms for hosted-primary via feature-flag
(devops-bot): feature-flag update OK
alex: monitoring... p95 dropping. 10:18 -> p95 at 320ms, 10:22 -> back to baseline ~190ms. queue depth back down. :thumbsup:
sam: captured profile after mitigations — kernel_init time eliminated, batch sizes recovered to mean ~5, KV eviction ratio down to 0.06.
tony: follow-ups: add regression test to catch kselector flip causing aux kernel fallback for short batches; add a canary gate for adaptive-kselector changes; improve KV cache priming telemetry to correlate evictions -> priming cost.
jen: filing GH issues: GH#4321 (kselector canary), GH#4322 (sampler regression test), GH#4323 (kv-priming metric).
alex: good work. noting timeline for postmortem and action items. closing thread once postmortem PR lands.
jen: closing after PR, will include the small flame snippet and perf numbers in postmortem.
alex: resolved — reverting heuristics-optimizer rollout flagged in release notes. :white_check_mark:
